newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman bourse falls despite some select demand.
newsitem.headline: Amman bourse falls despite some select demand.

text.p: Jordan's stockmarket fell at the end of weekly trade on Wednesday in absence of strong foreign orders to help it resume last month's upward trend, dealers said.
Strong buying by mostly Gulf Arab investors on Jordan Kuwait Bank helped push the stock to the maximum five percent daily price ceiling, rising 0.20 dinars to 4.18 dinars.

Brokers said active trade in the bank, which alone accounted for a third of Wednesday's value, was linked to a power struggle between major shareholders to pre-empt a hostile takeover by Bank of Jordan, which owns a minority holding.

Brokers say the bourse is generally stable amid some foreign interest which resurfaced since Saturday but nowhere near the scale of an unprecedented emerging funds buying spree on cement and mining firms which the bourse witnessed last month.
Aside from some buying in Jordan Cement, suspected to be executed by foreign funds, there was hardly any significant demand on most of the traded stock on the official market, dealers said.
It shed 0.05 dinars to 4.07 dinars in the second busiest trade of the day worth 203,901 dinars.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.24 percent to 160.93 points in moderate turnover of 931,850 dinars.
There was also some demand on Jordan National Bank, which was unchanged at 2.13 dinars in 84,780 dinars worth of trade.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.17 percent to 81.78 points, 1.93 percent down from the start of the year.
